newsitem.title: UK: Return anticipated to cuts in sugar stocks - Merril.
newsitem.headline: Return anticipated to cuts in sugar stocks - Merril.

text.p: World sugar markets could see a return to a policy of stock reduction next year after difficulties exporting India's large stockpile, brokers Merrill Lynch said on Monday.

"With this year's projected surplus reduced because of the difficulties in India, the build in stocks is not as burdensome," analyst Judith Ganes said in Merrill Lynch's biweekly Commodity Market Trends report.
Assuming a two percent rise in global sugar consumption next season a return to stock reduction could occur, the report said.
India was unlikely to be a net sugar exporter in 1997/98 despite its adequate stocks as production was not expected to rebound due to a lack of government incentives to plant cane.
The size of Brazil's harvest and export potential greater than the announced plan would provide the one significant bearish feature for market prices, it said.
"This should keep prompt supplies from being tight and cap potential short term advances," it said.
But while the market had discounted much of the bearish news, it could still be surprised by sugar outputs which were lower than expected.
